gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named reviewer's measurement for any under-$100 pick: The Hook Up's side-by-side tests rank the VIOFO A119 Mini 2 against the Vantrue S1 Pro, and DashCamTalk tester rcg530 measured parking draw at about 2.05 W for the A119 Mini 2 against 0.21 W for Vantrue's collision-detection mode, which takes 9 to 12 s to start recording.
standout_why: Compared against carcody.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited), plus dealdey.com, dashcamempire.com, cabincommand.com and the visible part of digitalcameraworld.com. None carries a measured figure or names a tester. Carcody says its night notes are 'not standardized independent night tests', rottenwifi says it uses 'manufacturer specifications and listed price signals, not standardized independent lab testing', dealdey says 'We did not film footage with these cameras ourselves', and cabincommand says 'Nobody here has handled any of these cameras'. Digitalcameraworld says its author tested units, but the visible part gives no figures and none of ChatGPT's picks. Two pages could not be opened: dashanddrive.com (cited; TLS certificate error) and caranddriver.com (fetch blocked), so standout is held at 2.
decides: It confirms the VIOFO A119 Mini 2 as the tested front-only pick only when it sells under $100: The Hook Up bought it at $98.99 (2024) and $85 (2025), but VIOFO's US store search listed it at $159.99 on 2026-11-21. At today's prices the Vantrue S1 Pro 1CH ($79.99 in the partner table) is the under-$100 camera with a named side-by-side against it. The Hook Up called the two 'almost identical' by day, gave the Vantrue a slight edge on a passing plate, and found the VIOFO's HDR better tuned for plates at night. That test used the 2-channel S1 Pro at $159.99, so it carries over only if the 1CH front camera is the same. For parked cars the trade-off is measured: Vantrue's collision detection draws about a tenth of the A119 Mini 2's power but starts 9 to 12 s after the hit, while the VIOFO keeps 15 s from before the trigger. No named measurement was found for the 70mai A400, REDTIGER A2 or Rexing V1 Lite, so those ChatGPT picks rest on maker specs only.

findings.label: Parking-mode energy use, measured by The Hook Up
findings.value: about 0.35 Wh per 30 minutes in impact-based parking recording; 1.15 Wh per 30 minutes in low-bitrate recording
findings.source_title: Best Dashcams 2025 – The Clear Winner After Testing 13 Models (The Hook Up, 2025-12-19)
findings.note: 1-channel, front only. Arithmetic: 0.35 Wh / 0.5 h = 0.7 W average; 1.15 Wh / 0.5 h = 2.3 W average. The article does not describe the meter or the hardwire kit. The impact-mode figure is lower than rcg530's 2.05 W for 'Auto Event Detection' on 2023 firmware; modes and firmware differ.

findings.label: Overall placing in The Hook Up's 13-camera test, and price it paid
findings.source_title: Best Dashcams 2025 – The Clear Winner After Testing 13 Models (The Hook Up, 2025-12-19)
findings.note: Cameras were compared four at a time, day and night, on plates with both cars stationary, both moving, and a car passing. In round 1, moving by day, it did not give a 100% legible plate. Moving at night it was second to the $169 70mai M800, and 'none of the cameras produced a legible plate'. Rankings are the reviewer's judgement of footage, not instrument readings.

findings.label: The Hook Up's 2024 verdict for budgets under $100
findings.value: 'the $98 Viofo A119 Mini 2 is miles ahead of other cameras in the price range'; ranked 4th for daytime video and 3rd for night video
findings.source_title: Ultimate Dash Cam Comparison 2024 (The Hook Up, 2024-12-19)
findings.note: Ten cameras, priced from $69.99 to $399. The article notes that in parking modes the A119 Mini 2 'uses a lower resolution and cropped field of view'. The fetch summary placed the day and night ranks among the finalists; confirm the group size on the page before quoting them.

findings.label: The Hook Up's side-by-side against the VIOFO A119 Mini 2
findings.value: By day 'the Vantrue S1 Pro and Viofo A119 Mini 2 where almost identical'; the Vantrue was 'ever so slightly better' on a passing car's plate, 'though neither produced a completely legible plate'; at night 'the Viofo's HDR seemed to be better tuned for capturing plates'
findings.source_title: Ultimate Dash Cam Comparison 2024 (The Hook Up, 2024-12-19)
findings.note: The unit tested was the 2-channel S1 Pro (front plus 1080p rear) at $159.99; only front footage is discussed. The under-$100 item today is the S1 Pro 1CH, front only. The S1 Pro was not in that article's final ranking.

findings.label: The Hook Up's plate result for the cheapest camera in its 2024 test
findings.value: $69.99; 'captured blurry images of even the easiest to read plates'
findings.source_title: Ultimate Dash Cam Comparison 2024 (The Hook Up, 2024-12-19)
findings.note: This is not the 70mai A400 that ChatGPT showed. It is the only named test of a sub-$100 70mai found, so it does not transfer to the A400.

findings.label: Parking-mode power draw, measured by rcg530 (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 2.05 W in Auto Event Detection while waiting, 2.08 W while recording (15 s before and 30 s after the trigger); 2.03 W in 10 fps time-lapse; 2.10 W in low bitrate
findings.source_title: Dashcam with low power consumption in parking mode (timelapse), post #22 by rcg530, 2024-03-05
findings.note: Firmware v1.0_20230912, parking-mode GPS off. The post does not name the meter or say where power was measured. Arithmetic: 12 h parked at 2.05 W = 24.6 Wh, about 2.05 Ah from a 12 V battery.

findings.label: Parking-mode power draw, measured by rcg530 (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 0.21 W in collision detection, 9 s to start recording; 1.59 W in low bitrate (1080p 15 fps tested); 1.60 W in low frame rate
findings.source_title: Dashcam with low power consumption in parking mode (timelapse), post #22 by rcg530, 2024-03-05
findings.note: Same tester and list as the A119 Mini 2 row. Arithmetic: 12 h parked at 0.21 W = 2.5 Wh, about 0.21 Ah at 12 V, roughly a tenth of the A119 Mini 2's draw. The cost is a 9 s gap after the impact before recording starts. Partner table price $69.99 (read 2026-11-21).

findings.label: Parking-mode power draw, measured by rcg530 (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 0.21 W in collision detection (12 s to start recording); 1.41 W in quick-start collision detection (3 s); 4.33 W in motion detection with no motion, 4.46 W while recording; 3.88 W in low bitrate; 4.04 W in low frame rate
findings.source_title: Dashcam with low power consumption in parking mode (timelapse), post #22 by rcg530, 2024-03-05
findings.note: Measured on the 2-channel unit (front plus rear). The 1CH version at $79.99 is not in the list; its always-recording modes should draw less with one camera, but that is not measured.

findings.label: Parking impact-mode draw and trigger timing by brand, The Hook Up 2024
findings.value: Vantrue: 0.64 W in 2-channel and 0.99 W in 3-channel impact mode, recording from about 4.5 s after the impact; Viofo cameras: roughly double that draw, recording from roughly 15 s before the impact
findings.source_title: Ultimate Dash Cam Comparison 2024 (The Hook Up, 2024-12-19)
findings.note: Average draw over 10 minutes per mode. The article does not say which Vantrue model gave the 0.64 W figure (the 3-channel one is most likely the N4 Pro). It also reports both Viofo cameras were knocked off their mounts on side impacts in its 16-impact jig test.
